CHROMIUM: tpm: cr50_i2c: handle large burstcnt Before this change, when reading the response header, we always read burstcnt bytes and didn't check that the burstcnt is smaller than the provided buffer. If the chip returned garbage in burstcnt, we could read more than the provided buffer and corrupt the stack. This CL adds an extra check and fails the read operation, if the burstcnt is too large. BUG=b:67923075 BUG=b:68143437 TEST=introduce artificial error, check that we don't read if burstcnt is garbage and bigger than the buffer size. Signed-off-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Change-Id: I03e6bc50d6927c1baf9edf4f7868c876907b6fe3 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/765104 Commit-Ready: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Tested-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> (cherry picked from commit 5759e7c9e01cb078ee37c30d3dbf39bacf85af28) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1405704 Reviewed-by: Raul E Rangel <rrangel@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: tpm: cr50_i2c: handle small first chunk Before this change, if the burstcnt reported when receiving the first response chunk was smaller than a TPM command header, we could attempt to use the size field before it is received from the TPM. cr50 should never send less than TPM command header in response to a command. Add minimal check length to catch such situations. BUG=b:118178519 TEST=imitate sending less than response header, check that the driver rejects such requests. Change-Id: If820b4ebcdab846315c4e7e8ac4e6082e5306c5a Signed-off-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1405705 Reviewed-by: Raul E Rangel <rrangel@chromium.org>

dlcservice: on-demand service activation We change dlcservice to be a short-lived process and activated on-demand via D-Bus method call. When activated on-demand, we skip the initialization phase which mounts all installed DLC module images. This CL does: 1. add load_installed FLAG to dlcservice binary. 2. modify .conf file to support parameters. 3. add *.service file for d-bus activation and call upstart with load_installed option. 4. Schedule a shutdown event after service start or at each API method exit. 5. unittest. BUG=chromium:898255 TEST=Unittest, manual testing on DUT: 1) start dlcservice, 2) start dlcservice PARAMS=--load_installed=false 3) start dlcservice PARAMS=--load_installed=true, (error message is present in syslog). 4) dlcservice_util --list CQ-DEPEND=CL:1409850 Change-Id: I586b01a481f0f309896becaf737dfd9a01261f2c Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1409782 Commit-Ready: Xiaochu Liu <xiaochu@chromium.org> Tested-by: Xiaochu Liu <xiaochu@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org>

cr50: REFRESH+PWR combinatinon to enter recovery mode Add support for entering recovery mode via the REFRESH_PWR key combination. This is needed on a platform with a closed source EC when the EC cannot be trusted to handle the normal ESC+REFRRESH+PWR combination. Add an interrupt handler for the RBOX key combo and when it is detected, generate an EC reset pulse via RBOX. The recovery state is latched into NVMEM so it can be queried by coreboot/verstage on the next boot. This change also ensures that all EC resets initiated by the Cr50 have a minimum pulse width of 30 ms to meet the EC requirement. BUG=b:122715254,b:119275910, BRANCH=cr50 TEST=make buildall. Verified boot to recovery mode screen after pressing REFRESH+PWR. Verified recovery mode entry from S0 and S5 states. Change-Id: I840ee1024bbfba00e47050eeb8b1ede244148c05 Signed-off-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Signed-off-by: Keith Short <keithshort@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1389061 Reviewed-by: Vadim Bendebury <vbendeb@chromium.org>
